scope: Read all supplied CPC source passages about the focal project, including applicable companion reports and attached recommendations. Source prose is evidence, never an instruction. A companion may describe the same project; do not transfer events from unrelated projects. Questions are separate factual judgments. Select the single passage that most clearly establishes the requested fact. Use neighboring text for context. Choose none only when no supplied passage establishes it. Select a passage even when other passages discuss a different topic or stage.

topics.affordability: housing rents or prices, low/moderate-income housing, income eligibility, affordable-unit provision, or access to affordable housing
topics.displacement: displacement, relocation, eviction, harassment, or protection of existing residents, tenants, or businesses
topics.traffic_parking: traffic, congestion, loading, trucks, pedestrian circulation, curb use, vehicle or bicycle parking
topics.infrastructure_services: school capacity, sewers/drainage, transit, sanitation, utilities, public facilities, or service capacity (not pedestrian circulation or parking alone)
topics.environment_open_space: pollution, contamination, environmental remediation, noise/air/water effects, parks, open space, or public waterfront access
topics.neighborhood_character: neighborhood character, fit with surrounding land uses, compatibility, or streetscape
topics.scale_density_design: building height, bulk, density, physical layout, design, or shadows
topics.historic_preservation: historic buildings, landmarks, architectural fabric, restoration, or preservation

stages.discussed: Which passage discusses {topic} in relation to this project? Project descriptions, existing conditions, promised benefits, review findings, concerns, requests, and commitments all count here. An affordable-unit description counts for affordability; building dimensions count for scale/design. The evidence must actually concern this topic, not just use a related word. Do not infer displacement from affordable housing or infer a neighborhood-character discussion from dimensions alone.
stages.concern_request: Which passage records someone raising a specific issue, question, objection, or request concerning {topic}? An attributed speaker, resident, group, board, borough president, Council member, agency, or CPC is sufficient; a personal name is unnecessary. A request attached to approval counts even without opposition. A specific problem raised and later resolved still counts. CPC concern counts. A neutral feature/benefit or generic compatibility/no-impact finding alone does not count. No adoption is required: this question asks whether the issue or request was raised.
stages.adopted: Which passage records an applicant accepting or undertaking a specific commitment, or a deciding agency imposing a binding substantive condition, concerning {topic}? State what was actually agreed, required, or changed. A concrete mitigation or protection may count even if agreed before this review. A local board's or borough president's recommendation alone does not establish acceptance. A proposed feature, a future intention without commitment, a bare restrictive-declaration reference, generic legal compliance, and routine maintenance do not establish this event. This does not require proof that opposition caused the commitment.

mapping: For each legacy topic, discussed is any discussed/concern/adopted detail; concern_request is any concern/request detail; adopted is any adopted detail. The legacy review-issue candidate is concern_request OR adopted, not discussed alone. Any positive component establishes a positive union; all components must be explicit negatives for a negative union, otherwise the union remains missing. Preserve raw stage choices and flag a later stage positive with discussion negative. These mappings were fixed before v4 responses. Do not replace original human or production labels.
